subject.title: Workboard worktree dispatch bypasses the operator.admin gate on arbitrary-repo worktree creation (confused deputy)

question: Should Workboard require operator.admin at the point any card or board mutation persists an explicit managed-worktree host source path?
rationale: The expected boundary is supported by current docs and sibling Gateway contracts, but this is a public security-sensitive authorization report whose disclosure, backport, and temporary mitigation path require maintainer/security ownership.

options.title: Gate source paths at mutation time
options.body: Require operator.admin before persisting explicit Workboard worktree source paths and add regression proof that write-only callers cannot plant a later-materialized repo root.

options.title: Temporarily fail closed
options.body: Disable or reject Workboard managed-worktree materialization until the card-author authority path is audited and repaired.

options.title: Downgrade to hardening
options.body: Treat this as non-security hardening under the trusted-operator model, accepting that Workboard would remain inconsistent with the documented operator.write/operator.admin split.

recommendation.title: Gate source paths at mutation time
recommendation.body: Require operator.admin before persisting explicit Workboard worktree source paths and add regression proof that write-only callers cannot plant a later-materialized repo root.

likelyOwner.reason: The report concerns a security boundary and CODEOWNERS/SECURITY.md route this class of review through secops.
